params.q: Up to what income is there zero income tax under the new tax regime in India?

search_parameters.q: Up to what income is there zero income tax under the new tax regime in India?

response.markdown:
**Up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income** is tax-free under India's new tax regime (FY 2025-26 / AY 2026-27), thanks to the **₹60,000 rebate under Section 87A**, which wipes out the tax on income up to that level. [0] [1] [2] [3] [4]

For **salaried** taxpayers, the **₹75,000 standard deduction** pushes the zero-tax threshold to **₹12.75 lakh of gross salary**, since it reduces taxable income to ₹12 lakh. [1] [5] [6] [0] [7]

Key details:
- **Slab rates**: Nil up to ₹4L, 5% (₹4–8L), 10% (₹8–12L), 15% (₹12–16L), 20% (₹16–20L), 25% (₹20–24L), 30% above ₹24L. [7]
- **Marginal relief** applies just above ₹12 lakh, so you only pay tax on the amount exceeding ₹12 lakh. [1] [7] [0]
- The rebate applies only to **normal slab-rate income** — it does **not** cover special-rate income like capital gains, lottery, betting, or crypto. [2] [4]

Note: The Income Tax Department's older FAQ page still mentions ₹7 lakh (pre-FY 2025-26); the current limit under the revised regime is **₹12 lakh**. [2] [5]
